short: The Ikaros family (IKZF1 Ikaros, IKZF2 Helios, IKZF3 Aiolos, IKZF4 Eos, IKZF5 Pegasus) are lymphoid zinc-finger proteins with an N-terminal C2H2 array that binds DNA and a C-terminal pair of fingers that mediates homo- and heterodimerization. They recognize a GGGAA core, present in lymphocyte-specific regulatory elements and also in pericentromeric satellite repeats, to which Ikaros localizes by direct DNA binding. IKZF1 is required for the development of all lymphoid lineages, is deleted in BCR-ABL1 and Ph-like B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia where it predicts poor outcome, and, with IKZF3, is the protein whose thalidomide-analog-induced degradation explains how lenalidomide works in myeloma. The GGGAA core is shared with ETS and NF-kB sites, which makes these motifs hard to trust.
long:
## The factors

Five human Ikaros-family proteins are encoded by IKZF1 to IKZF5: Ikaros, Helios, Aiolos, Eos and
Pegasus. Each has an N-terminal array of C2H2 zinc fingers that binds DNA and a separate C-terminal
pair of fingers that is not used for DNA contact but mediates homodimerization and heterodimerization
among family members. Alternative splicing of IKZF1 produces isoforms (Ik-1 through Ik-5 in the
original description) carrying different combinations of the N-terminal fingers; these differ in
sequence specificity and affinity, with the full-length forms binding the whole set of recognition
sequences found in lymphocyte-specific regulatory elements and the short forms binding only a subset.
The short forms are also poorly nuclear and are weak activators, which is the basis of their
dominant-negative behavior.

Expression is lymphoid and largely restricted: IKZF1 and IKZF3 across B and T lineages, IKZF2 in
regulatory T cells and some other compartments, IKZF4 in regulatory T cells, IKZF5 more broadly.
Only IKZF1, IKZF2 and IKZF3 have motif models in the databases behind this family. The proteins work
in complexes rather than alone, associating with NuRD (Mi-2/CHD4) and with histone deacetylases, and
they localize to pericentromeric heterochromatin.

## The motif

The agreed core is GGGAA, written TTCCC on the other strand. Extended forms appear in the databases
as TGGGAATAC and similar; the representative archetype for this family has that consensus. None of
these carries much information beyond the five-base core, and that is the central problem for this
family, because GGGAA is not distinctive. It is contained within the ETS core GGA(A/T) and within the
NF-kB half-site GGGRNNYYCC, so an Ikaros matrix, an ETS matrix and an NF-kB matrix can all score the
same DNA.

The collection makes this concrete. The JASPAR IKZF3 matrix has the consensus CAGGAAGTG, whose
nearest neighbors across all four databases are ETS models rather than Ikaros models; the JASPAR
IKZF2 matrix, AGGAAG, likewise resembles ETS more than it resembles the rest of its own family; and
two Vierstra archetypes in this family are explicitly named for mixed groups, IKZF with ZNF and IKZF
with NFKB. Family cohesion is correspondingly low. Ikaros also binds within centromeric DNA repeats,
and targeting to pericentromeric foci depends on the DNA-binding finger domain together with the
dimerization domain, so part of the genuine binding repertoire is repetitive sequence that motif
scanners will report en masse.

## Where it acts

Ikaros-family sites are found at promoters and enhancers of lymphoid genes, including the
immunoglobulin and T-cell-receptor loci, and co-occur with EBF1, PU.1/SPI1, RUNX1 and E2A at B- and
T-lineage regulatory elements. Because PU.1 is itself an ETS factor that prefers a purine-rich GGAA
core, Ikaros and PU.1 sites are often indistinguishable in sequence at the same elements, and
composite occupancy is common. The other distinctive location is pericentromeric heterochromatin,
where Ikaros accumulates in foci; this was shown to require direct DNA binding rather than
recruitment through Mi-2, and is consistent with Ikaros sites inside satellite repeats. Genome-wide,
a five-base core occurs on the order of a million times, so scanning alone cannot define an Ikaros
cistrome.

## Biology and disease

Ikzf1-null mice lack B cells and have profound defects across lymphoid lineages, establishing IKZF1
as required for the development of all lymphoid lineages; mice expressing dominant-negative isoforms
develop T-cell leukemia. In humans, focal deletions and point mutations of IKZF1 are a defining
feature of BCR-ABL1-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and of Ph-like ALL, and IKZF1
deletion is associated with a substantially worse outcome, which is why it is now assayed in risk
stratification. Germline dominant-negative IKZF1 variants cause a combined T-, B- and myeloid-cell
immunodeficiency, and other IKZF1 variants cause common variable immunodeficiency.

The best-known pharmacology is degradation, not transcription. Thalidomide, lenalidomide and
pomalidomide act as molecular glues that recruit a zinc finger of IKZF1 and IKZF3 to cereblon, the
substrate receptor of the CRL4-CRBN ubiquitin ligase, causing their selective degradation; this
accounts for the activity of these drugs in multiple myeloma. A systematic screen of the human C2H2
zinc-finger proteome identified eleven such degrons and predicted that more than 150 zinc fingers can
engage the drug-CRBN interface, which turned the Ikaros story into a general strategy for targeting
zinc-finger transcription factors.

## Reading a hit

Treat an Ikaros hit as a weak, ambiguous call. Three problems stack. First, the informative core is
five bases, so matches are everywhere. Second, that core is shared with ETS and NF-kB, and the
databases themselves are contaminated: at least one JASPAR Ikaros matrix in this family is closer to
ETS models than to Ikaros models, and two archetypes are named for IKZF together with ZNF or NFKB.
If you get an Ikaros hit at a lymphoid enhancer, PU.1 or another ETS factor is at least as likely to
be the direct binder. Third, no sequence argument distinguishes IKZF1 from IKZF2 or IKZF3, and IKZF4
and IKZF5 have no models here. Ikaros models are ChIP- and selection-derived in these collections
rather than backed by a structure of the protein on DNA, and Ikaros works in NuRD and HDAC complexes,
so indirect binding is a live possibility for any individual peak. A credible Ikaros call needs
lineage-appropriate expression, a peak from a well-controlled experiment, and ideally loss of the
peak on IKZF1 degradation rather than a motif match.
caveats: The informative core is only GGGAA, which is shared with ETS (GGAA) and NF-kB (GGGAA) sites, so an Ikaros match is rarely attributable to an Ikaros protein. The databases show the contamination directly: the JASPAR IKZF3 matrix here has ETS models as its nearest neighbors across all four sources, the IKZF2 matrix also resembles ETS more than its own family, and two Vierstra archetypes are named IKZF/ZNF and IKZF/NFKB. Family cohesion is low as a result. No model distinguishes IKZF1 from IKZF2 or IKZF3, and IKZF4 and IKZF5 have none. Ikaros additionally binds satellite repeats and acts within NuRD and HDAC complexes, so peaks need not reflect its own specificity.
